steps.say: The unified FIGO 2014 staging system applies identically to primary epithelial malignancies arising from the ovaries, fallopian tubes, and peritoneum. Formal surgical staging encompasses exploratory laparotomy, peritoneal washings, total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and infracolic omentectomy.
steps.tx: The unified **FIGO 2014 staging** system classifies neoplasms of the ovaries, fallopian tubes, and primary peritoneum together. Definitive **surgical staging** requires peritoneal cytology washings, total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, infracolic omentectomy, peritoneal biopsies, and retroperitoneal nodal evaluation.  Evidence-based practice integrates operative staging, fallopian tube primary, peritoneal primary.

nodes.label: Perform vertical midline laparotomy and aspirate ascites/washings
Perform total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
Harvest peritoneal surface biopsies (diaphragm, paracolic, pelvis)
Dissect pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes up to renal veins

steps.say: Stage one ovarian carcinoma remains strictly confined to the ovaries or fallopian tubes. Stage one A involves a single intact ovary, stage one B involves both ovaries with intact capsules, and stage one C represents capsular rupture or malignant cells in peritoneal cytology.
steps.tx: **Stage I** disease is limited to the ovaries or fallopian tubes: **Stage IA** involves one ovary with capsule intact; **Stage IB** involves both ovaries with intact capsules; and **Stage IC** denotes **capsular rupture** (IC1 intraoperative, IC2 pre-operative) or malignant cells in peritoneal washings (IC3).  Evidence-based practice integrates Stage IC1 intraoperative rupture, Stage IC2 surface tumor, Stage IC3 positive washings.

rows: Capsule intact, no tumor on surface
Capsule ruptured prior to surgery / surface tumor

steps.say: Stage two designates tumor extension below the pelvic brim or direct involvement of pelvic peritoneal surfaces. Substage two A involves the uterus or fallopian tubes, while substage two B extends to other pelvic intraperitoneal tissues such as the bladder peritoneum, pouch of Douglas, or sigmoid colon.
steps.tx: **Stage II** designates tumor extending beyond the ovaries with pelvic extension below the pelvic brim: **Stage IIA** reflects extension or implants on the **uterus or fallopian tubes**, while **Stage IIB** reflects extension to other pelvic intraperitoneal tissues including rectum, bladder, and pelvic peritoneum.  Evidence-based practice integrates Stage IIA pelvic extension, Stage IIB pelvic intraperitoneal tissues. Key numerical parameters include 2.

left.title: Stage IIA Disease
points: Direct extension or implants on uterus
Involvement of ipsilateral or contralateral fallopian tube
Confined strictly to genital internal pelvic viscera

right.title: Stage IIB Disease
points: Direct spread to pouch of Douglas, bladder wall, or sigmoid
Still confined entirely below the true pelvic brim

steps.say: Stage three involves confirmed peritoneal metastases outside the pelvis or retroperitoneal lymph node spread. Substage three A one identifies isolated retroperitoneal nodal metastasis, divided by size into subcentimeter or exceeding ten millimeters.
steps.tx: **Stage IIIA1** designates retroperitoneal **lymph node metastasis** confirmed pathologically with microscopic or absent extrapelvic peritoneal spread: **Stage IIIA1(i)** defines metastasis <=10 mm largest dimension, whereas **Stage IIIA1(ii)** defines nodal metastasis >10 mm dimension.  Evidence-based practice integrates Stage IIIA1 retroperitoneal nodes, cutoff 10 mm (i vs ii), Stage IIIA2 microscopic extrapelvic. Key numerical parameters include 3, 2.

nodes.label: Pathological dissection of pelvic and para-aortic nodes
Measure maximum diameter of metastatic nodal deposit

steps.say: Macroscopic peritoneal carcinomatosis outside the pelvic brim stratifies Stage three B and Stage three C disease based on physical deposit size. Deposits up to two centimeters designate three B, while deposits exceeding two centimeters designate Stage three C.
steps.tx: Extrapelvic peritoneal metastases establish **Stage IIIA2** (microscopic peritoneal spread), **Stage IIIB** (macroscopic peritoneal metastasis <=2 cm largest diameter), and **Stage IIIC** (macroscopic **peritoneal metastasis** >2 cm, including tumor extension to liver or spleen capsule without parenchymal invasion).  Evidence-based practice integrates Stage IIIB <=2 cm peritoneal, Stage IIIC >2 cm peritoneal, liver/spleen surface capsule. Key numerical parameters include 3.

steps.say: Stage four reflects distant dissemination beyond the peritoneal cavity. Pleural effusion with cytologically proven malignant cells designates Stage four A, while parenchymal metastases to liver or spleen or extra-abdominal organ involvement defines Stage four B.
steps.tx: **Stage IVA** requires cytologically proven **malignant pleural effusion**. **Stage IVB** identifies distant dissemination including parenchymal liver or spleen metastases, transmural intestinal invasion, inguinal lymph node metastasis, or distant hematogenous extra-abdominal visceral spread.  Evidence-based practice integrates Stage IVA pleural effusion cytology, Stage IVB parenchymal metastases, extra-abdominal nodes. Key numerical parameters include 4.

left.title: Stage IVA Dissemination
points: Benign reactive pleural effusions do not qualify

steps.say: High-grade serous carcinoma accounts for seventy percent of epithelial ovarian cancers and universally harbors TP53 mutations. Emerging from serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma in the fimbriated fallopian tube, these tumors are characterized by profound homologous recombination deficiency.
steps.tx: **High-grade serous carcinoma** (HGSC) accounts for ~70% of cases, arising from **serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma** (STIC) in the fallopian tube fimbria. HGSC universally harbors **TP53 mutations** (96%), demonstrates profound chromosomal instability, and exhibits homologous recombination deficiency in 50% of tumors.  Evidence-based practice integrates Type I tumors, stepwise progression, KRAS BRAF PTEN ARID1A, low-grade indolent. Key numerical parameters include 1, 2.

nodes.label: Precursor STIC lesion arises in fallopian tube fimbrial epithelium
Acquisition of early pathogenic TP53 mutation (p53 signature)
Malignant fimbrial cells shed onto ovarian cortical surface
Rapid intra-abdominal carcinomatosis with high chromosomal instability

steps.say: Endometrioid and clear cell carcinomas frequently arise from pre-existing ovarian endometriosis and display distinctive molecular aberrations. Clear cell tumors harbor ARID1A mutations, whereas low-grade serous tumors arise from serous borderline precursors and carry KRAS mutations.
steps.tx: Non-HGSC subtypes display distinct biology: **clear cell carcinoma** (hobnail cells, ARID1A and PIK3CA mutations, platinum chemoresistance, thromboembolism risk); **endometrioid carcinoma** (arises in endometriosis, PTEN and beta-catenin mutations); and **low-grade serous carcinoma** (KRAS/BRAF mutations, indolent biology).  Evidence-based practice integrates Type II tumors, TP53 >95%, chromosomal instability, HRD pathway.

rows: Often stage I; poor response to platinum
